text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has ordered the Sabah state government to investigate why rampant log smuggling out of the state has gone undetected, mentioning the case of seven ships which loaded logs said to be bound for Japan.
-- Malaysian Airlines said it has taken steps to address its immediate and long-term problems, referring to reports it was facing a manpower shortage and that service standards have fallen.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad in Tokyo, has invited Japanese companies to invest in Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor.
-- Credit card issuers were reluctant to say whether a recent move by Hongkong Bank (Malaysia) to lower its card fees would force others to follow suit, but acknowledge that margins were thinning.
-- Kedah state chief minister Sanusi Junid said he has ordered investigations into how some 15,000 hectares of land went "missing" despite being gazetted as permannent forest reserve in the state.
